publication_title: Enterprise Content Marketing Benchmarks, Budgets, and Trends: 2025 Research
sample: 310 enterprise-marketer respondents, mostly from North America; a subset of 1,186 global survey responses
metric: 47% of enterprise marketers cited managing workflow issues or the content approval process as a situational challenge
summary: Content approval friction appears in the survey as a reported enterprise marketing challenge.
caveat: Self-reported survey, not a causal estimate or proof that the proposed platform solves the problem.

publication_title: Enterprise Content Marketing Benchmarks, Budgets, and Trends: 2025 Research
sample: 310 enterprise-marketer respondents, mostly from North America; a subset of 1,186 global survey responses
metric: 61% cited communication across organisational silos as a situational challenge
summary: Cross-team communication is a common reported challenge in this enterprise-marketer sample.
caveat: Same survey and respondents as EVID-01; do not count it as independent research or generalise the percentage to every organisation.

publication_title: Enterprise Content Marketing Benchmarks, Budgets, and Trends: 2025 Research
sample: 310 enterprise-marketer respondents, mostly from North America; a subset of 1,186 global survey responses
metric: 75% reported that their organisation used generative AI; 62% said their organisation had generative AI usage guidelines
summary: AI use and formal guidance coexist in this sample, supporting investigation of review workflows for AI-assisted content.
caveat: Self-reported survey. The two percentages are not a measured link between AI use and brand errors.

publication_title: GOV.UK content principles: conventions and research background
sample: Published research background and guidance; no survey sample for this statement
summary: The publication explains that when many people originate content, a style guide supplies shared decisions on wording, format, and accuracy and supports consistent presentation.
caveat: Qualitative rationale from a public-sector guidance document, not measured evidence of this product or a current estimate of commercial brand losses.
